trust_decision.summary: Decided: a chat row may only be persisted with a folder_id on which the caller holds write access (owner, an access grant, or inheritance up the folder's parent chain); enforced in the chat-creation and chat-move handlers, with the check itself in the shared access-control module.

landing_point.why: The only new-chat insert in the chat-completions handler, persisting folder_id taken straight from the request body (main.py:1202, :1328). An engineer reading 'inject chats into another user's folder via chat completions' starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/chat/completions (alias /api/v1/chat/completions); check absent at pinned commit, added by fix.diff:22-27
POST /api/v1/chats/new; inline owner/shared-write check already present at pinned commit, folded into the shared helper by fix.diff:63-67
POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/folder; inline owner/shared-write check already present at pinned commit, folded into the shared helper by fix.diff:87-91
has_folder_write_access() called from all three handlers above; new function in backend/open_webui/utils/access_control/folders.py

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Fork/clone/import copy a folder_id already stored on a chat the caller owns or may read, so a solver can argue those paths add no caller-supplied folder reference and leave them unguarded.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A chat may legitimately be placed in a folder the caller does not own but holds a 'write' grant on (AccessGrants) or inherits from an ancestor folder via parent_id; and folder_id=None must keep moving a chat out of any folder. An ownership-only guard (folder.user_id == user.id) rejects both.

O6_input_shapes: new-chat shape: parent_id present as null and chat_id absent, which is what makes is_new_chat true (backend/open_webui/main.py:1151)
folder_id absent or null: no check, chat persisted with a NULL folder_id (fix.diff:86-87)
foreign, non-existent or non-UUID folder_id: 404 NOT_FOUND (fix.diff:22-27)
another user's folder granted to the caller with 'write': must pass, via AccessGrants (backend/open_webui/utils/access_control/folders.py:11-18)
child folder whose write access is inherited from an ancestor: must pass, via the parent_id walk (backend/open_webui/utils/access_control/folders.py:19-23)
move shape: folder_id null on POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/folder moves the chat out of any folder (backend/open_webui/routers/chats.py:2128-2136)
message_ids supplied as a list, a legacy dict, or a single id, all of which still reach the new-chat insert (backend/open_webui/main.py:1157-1167)
db supplied as a live session on the two router paths vs omitted (db=None default) on the completions path (fix.diff:104, fix.diff:114)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/v1/chats/{id}/fork persists the source chat's folder_id through Chats.insert_new_chat with no write-access check and no clearing; only chat.import permission is required (defaults true, config.py:1881)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It copies a folder_id already stored on the caller's own chat, so it reads as a copy of existing state rather than a new caller-controlled folder reference.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package from the landing point; a file the fix touched for other hunks but never for fork

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a write-access precondition inside Chats.insert_new_chat so every caller inherits it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Six call sites share this constructor (main.py, fork, notes x2, timers, subagents, automations); a maintainer consolidating authorisation into one place would put it here rather than in six handlers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a folder-delete or folder-merge path that rewrites chats into a caller-chosen target folder_id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: delete_folder_by_id already calls move_chats_by_user_id_and_folder_id with a target argument (backend/open_webui/routers/folders.py:692 passes None); offering 'move chats to another folder' is a natural feature and would bypass every handler-level check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a clone route that copies folder_id instead of relying on import_chats to drop it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Clone already copies pinned/variables/meta from the source chat, so copying folder_id in the folder-shared case is the obvious next field to add.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a has_folder_write_access-style helper reused by notes, knowledge and automations chats
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tree is already converging on this module (routers/folders.py, utils/middleware.py, retrieval/utils.py import it), so a new resource-level check belongs there, not in each handler.

O9_family: Authorization / IDOR: missing write-ownership check on a user-controlled foreign key (CWE-639, CWE-862)

O10_build.language: Python (FastAPI backend) + Svelte/Node frontend, frontend not needed for this path
O10_build.toolchain: Python 3.11+, pip/uv with backend/requirements.txt, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, SQLite by default (backend/open_webui/env.py:267)
O10_build.project_tests: none for this area: the backend has no test suite at the pinned commit (no test_*.py under backend/), and the fix diff adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the /chats/new ownership test into main.py alone (folder.user_id == user.id, or Folders.get_folder_by_id_and_user_id), which rejects legitimate new chats in folders shared with write access and leaves the other create/copy paths on their own checks.

out_of_scope_notes: Folder-level permission checks in routers/folders.py (e.g. :154 for creating in a parent folder, :497 for updating a folder's access grants) are adjacent to but outside this advisory's chat->folder write property; noted and not examined.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session); the tree is clearly large (backend + frontend), far above the 5 MB tiny_repo line and not obviously near 1.5 GB.

Whether the new guard is reachable offline: /api/chat/completions resolves a model from app.state.MODELS before the check (backend/open_webui/main.py:1071-1083), so that path needs a configured local or fake OpenAI-compatible provider; /chats/new and /chats/{id}/folder are pure DB and need none.

Whether the Anthropic-compat endpoints can carry folder_id: convert_anthropic_to_openai_payload forwards unknown parameters only when an admin sets passthrough_params to '*' (backend/open_webui/utils/anthropic.py:381-394), so /api/v1/messages is normally not a separate route into the same sink.
